newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks turn to fall in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks turn to fall in late trade.

text.p: Taiwan share prices reversed early gains to fall slightly in late Tuesday amid caution after the central bank took moves to tighten liquidity, brokers said.
With 40 minutes left, at 0320 GMT, the index was down 15.41 points or 0.17 percent at 9,307.43, off a 9,371.50 high.
Turnover was a brisk T$126 billion.

"The caution is giving face to the central bank," said indepedent analyst Michael Hung. "If the index rises further after gaining so much recently, the central bank might take tougher moves to cool the market."
The central bank on Monday issued T$11 billion negotiable certificates of deposit to mop up excess money, a move widely seen as aiming to cool the red-hot stock market.
Financials, constructions and plastics fell, but electronics were up 0.18 percent, with chipmaker Winbond, the market's most heavily traded share, up T$2 to T$60.5.
Hung said he expected a short period of consolidation between 9,000 and 9,400 points in the near term.
